chunks: And Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام, when he intended to relieve himself, would stand at the door of the place, then turn to his right and to his left toward his two angels and say: “Move away from me; for you two, by Allah, I am bound not to speak with my tongue anything until I come out to you.”

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: The title of Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib عليه السلام, meaning Commander of the Faithful
key_terms.الْحَاجَةَ: Relieving oneself; going to fulfill a bodily need
key_terms.بَابِ الْمَذْهَبِ: The entrance to the place used for relieving oneself
key_terms.مَلَكَيْهِ: His two angels, i.e., the recording angels

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali عليه السلام say before entering the place of relieving himself?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the etiquette of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام when entering the place of relieving oneself. It highlights modesty, awareness of the recording angels, and refraining from speech in such a setting.
